utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The indication is in the top left corner of this decision. Do you recognise, General, the stamp on this decision?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it the stamp of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Defence Ministry of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this decision -- has this decision been signed by the Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command, Sefer Halilovic, and the President of the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. Alija Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what it is stated here, that they signed it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, does this decision refer to the temporary organisation and formation of units of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it a decision on the formation of the temporary command of JUD, "South", based in the broader area of Igman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please now look at the second document, General? The date of the second document is identical to the date on the previous document, that is the 20th August, 1992. Is that not so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The body issuing this appointment is the staff of the Supreme Command of the armed forces Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On this document too we see the stamp of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, is that not so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This document too has been signed by the Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and by the President of the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, General, that this document appoints the temporary command, consisting of 11 persons as indicated in this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that under point 3 of this document it is stated that Delalic Zejnil has been appointed "Assistant Commander for Logistics"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could the General now be shown document 187 and 190 of the Prosecution, which were shown to the General yesterday? General, have you had time to look at these documents that you were shown yesterday when you were asked questions by my learned colleague?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let us first look at the document dated 28th August 1992. It is a request for saving meals for the needs of the Igman units. This document was issued by the Commander of the Tactical Group 1, Zejnil Delalic, is that not so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, General, that in view of the fact that on August 20th, 1992, by special appointment, Mr. Zejnil Delalic was appointed assistant commander for logistics, that this authorisation for meals for the army in Group JUD emanated from his responsibilities stemming from this appointment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what is stated in the heading of the request for operation codename "South".

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, General, if in answer to the question of my learned colleague you said that this could be something that conveys the contents of the duties of the Commander, then that would not be quite precise, because at the time you did not know that Mr. Delalic had been appointed precisely as assistant for logistics for the operation "South"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but maybe he had not been relieved of the duty of command of the Tactical Group. He may have still been Commander of the Tactical Group; and in that case he may also act as a Commander, as well as a logistics Commander in the group.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is precisely why I have put to you certain questions. Therefore, continuing to perform the duties of Commander of the Tactical Group, he was given additional assignments on the basis of this appointment to the temporary command of the Group "South"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It emerges as such from the documents and Mr. Delalic himself knows best.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Now look at the second document that you reviewed yesterday too, and which is dated 13th September, 1992. This document too was issued by Mr. Zejnil Delalic, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the authorisations given to Mr. Delalic as assistant commander for logistics of the temporary command of the Group "South", is it normal for Mr. Delalic to concern himself and to deal with problems that arose in the logistics area in all areas, not just meals, but also armaments, which this document refers to when he addresses the municipal staff. Was that within his responsibilities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All I can say is what is stated in the documents. If you want an expert opinion from me as a soldier, then that is something else. In this case, we do not have a document showing that Commander Delalic was relieved of the duty of Commander of the Tactical Group; and he was appointed to the Group JUD as assistant for logistics. Therefore, his Tactical Group is -- has become part of the Group JUD, at least a part of it, and within that Group he is assistant for logistics. Therefore -- but his command -- his role of Commander of Tactical Group, he has to regulate other matters within his area of responsibility, such as the question of the passage of these resources and equipment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General, that is precisely what I am trying to say. Mr. Delalic is the Commander of the Tactical Group at that time, but by this appointment he was given additional assignments within the temporary command of Group JUD?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I should now like to propose, your Honours, since the witness has interpreted the contents of these documents and recognised them too, identified them, I should like to tender these documents as evidence for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No objections, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Pasalic -- I apologise -- General, yesterday, in the course of your examination-in-chief, we saw a part of the interview that you granted in December 1992 to the local Jablanica TV station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also yesterday you identified the warrant for the arrest of a certain number of persons with the possibility of holding them in custody up to 30 days, and you also identified the criminal charges against Zejnil Delalic and Zdravko Mucic, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also yesterday you testified in this courtroom that you did so on the basis of the knowledge you had at the time, and that you were not prejudging things, because, if I may add to what you said, like any serious and responsible person you felt that the truth should be established by the court. Is that not so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You confirmed in this Trial Chamber that when you had learned about certain problems in Konjic immediately after being appointed Commander of the 4th Corps, you set up a commission to investigate those rumours, is that not so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge and ability you elected to the commission people who had capabilities that corresponded to the tasks assigned to them, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All your knowledge about the findings of the commission is based on the information given to you by that commission, is that not so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You personally did not conduct the investigations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not. Personally, no, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Everything that you investigated at the time, you combined that all and compiled criminal charges and you conveyed all that you knew to the public -- to the military prosecutor in Mostar, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The whole case, the whole file was compiled, which was quite a lengthy one, and from that file we concluded that criminal charges should be brought and warrants issued for the arrest of these people who had left the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore the competent bodies, and I assume that the criminal charges were written also by persons from the commission and not you personally, they did so on the basis of all the findings of the commission that was acting on your orders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you told us yesterday, you signed those criminal charges?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not say that I had signed them. It was signed by my deputy in my absence, but my name is there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Attached to the criminal charges was evidence in support of those criminal charges?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was submitted to the district military prosecutor's office in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, you personally did not examine the documents which the commission had insight into while performing its task, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I reviewed the entire file, together with the assistant for legal affairs, who headed the commission in the investigations. When I say that I reviewed it, it does not mean that I studied it in detail, and upon his proposal that criminal charges should be brought, I approved those charges and addressed them to the district military public prosecutor's office, with the approval of the Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the General be shown, again, exhibit D137, which was shown to this witness by the Prosecution yesterday? While waiting for the document, I know, General, that this assignment too was carried out under very difficult conditions of wartime and that you did everything you could at the time to clear up things there, and that in addition to the numerous other tasks that you had as the Corps Commander you relied on what, on the proposals made to you by the members of the commission, is that not so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, in answer to a question by my learned colleague Mr. Niemann, you said that for some persons you had indicated their positions, for others you did not. I should now like to ask you, in addition to this document, to see another document which the Defence received from the Prosecution, under the disclosure procedure, and which, according to the allegations of the Prosecutor, they obtained from the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I have a sufficient number of copies, both for the court and for you. They have been translated into English, so could they be, please, shown to the General after being identified?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence document D81/1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, this document, which is a document of the Supreme Command staff, do you recognise it by its contents as appointments for persons to Tactical Group 2?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This document is dated 14th August and does it say that Edib Saric has been appointed to Tactical Group 2?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When a moment ago we looked at the appointment for the temporary command of Group JUD, "South", under point 4 it was stated that the temporary command of Group JUD includes also Edib Saric for chief of security, did you notice that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In December 1992, General, you probably did not have occasion to see these documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not have occasion to see them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, you accepted the position of Edib Saric as you were informed of it by the members of the commission, is that not so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Yesterday, General, you were shown the criminal charges signed by your deputy on your behalf. Could the General now be shown, once again, the criminal charges brought against Zejnil Delalic and Zdravko Mucic of 22nd December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 141.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the criminal charges that you saw yesterday, and that you identified yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, General, that these criminal charges were submitted on 22nd December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the date indicated.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that these criminal charges were submitted against Zejnil Delalic and Zdravko Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, General, that attached to these criminal charges was supporting evidence indicated in the charges and which the commission had at its disposal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the task for the assistant for legal affairs and I think he carried out that task.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please look at page 2 of these criminal charges, where you will see proof in connection with the killing of Esad Bubalo, and we have the statement of Hazim Delic, deputy commander of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the description of the act.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, before that, below the description, it says "proof"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And it says, "statement of Hazim Delic, deputy commander of the Celebici prison"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that there is absolutely no other proof mentioned here, except that one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is no other here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true also that on page 3 under the heading "proof" and in relation to the offence by Zdravko Mucic we also find, "statement by the deputy commander of the Celebici prison, Hazim Delic"; is it correct that that is what it says?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, General, that under the heading "proof" there is no other proof listed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, General, that on page 2, where it says "description of the offence", there is a date that is on 31st February, 1992, Zejnil Delalic issued by telephone the order to liquidate this person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It says here the date here is 31st May.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that there is no position indicated for Mr. Zejnil Delalic here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do not believe this is really a form of objection, it is just a matter I wish to raise. That is that at all stages I have made it clear that the issue of the charges and the criminal proceedings is not a matter that the Prosecution had intended in any way to go into, and we were merely seeking to tender the evidence on the basis of the description of the titles that were contained in it. I wish to raise the issue that if counsel in cross-examination does, however, open up this subject then the approach that we have taken on this may well change, and I just wish to inform the Chamber that the basis upon which we sought to tender and the basis upon which we sought to proceed was predicated on an assumption that the Defence would not want to open up this issue for consideration by this Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the basis on which I am putting these questions in the cross-examination is precisely the position that my learned colleague has referred to. The General has just confirmed that in the description of the offence of Mr. Zejnil Delalic on 31st May, 1992, there is no indication of position.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, your Honour, with regard to what Mr. Niemann has just said I want to make it very clear for the record that Mr. Esad Landzo objects to any inquiry regarding this matter. We believe it is irrelevant to this proceeding and we therefore object to it. I also notice that it is 5.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Mr. Delic would also join that, would also say if substantive evidence is brought in we will be asking for a severance, a mid-trial severance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I suppose the Prosecution has made its position very clear. It now depends on the Defence to define its own position. Actually I did not think it was necessary to cross-examine along those lines, because it is completely irrelevant to what is being done here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecutor is charging my client of being Commander of the Tactical Group from the beginning of May, and he has indicated for what purpose he has questioned the witness in connection with this document. I just wanted to clarify, and the witness has confirmed, that in this document the position of Zejnil Delalic is not indicated. That is on the 31st May. Second, and my last question in connection with this document, is the position of Mr. Delalic was indicated as of the date 24th November, when as Commander of the Tactical Group he left Konjic, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I have no further questions in connection with this, and in view of the time I would ask the court to instruct us as to whether we can continue on Monday?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, it is obvious as long as you are still cross-examining you will continue on Monday when we resume at 10 o'clock. The Trial Chamber will rise.
